title: Who wrote Raeburn's early book: Harry Klee and Eddie Finckel
summary: Schremp asks who wrote for the first Raeburn band; Handy knew mainly Finckel.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: When you first ran into Raeburn, at that point Eddie was writing for the band, the first phase, and who else; do you remember who had contributed some stuff? Harry Klee wrote some things, it seems to me.
I didn't know that Harry wrote.
I think his name is on "Boyd's Nest". I may be wrong about that, but I believe his name is on top of "Boyd's Nest."
This comes as a shock to me right now. I had no idea that Harry could write, much less that he wrote that.
I'll look at it carefully when I get home; I certainly won't vouch for it because a lot of that stuff I haven't looked at for a while.
It could have been a sax solo by Harry Klee and maybe that part got left out.
of the parts. Maybe Junior was there. Anyway, Finkle wrote most of that book, I guess.
I think so, at that time. I don't know who the other guys were that he was using. The only one that I was aware of was Ed Finkle.
